title: Why the read path got faster
subtitle: What changed in the order lookup and what it costs

sections.title: Order lookups are served from memory, so reads no longer wait on the database
sections.text: A small cache sits in front of the orders table. Most reads never reach it.
points: The cache holds the 10,000 most recent orders.
A write removes the cached copy, so a reader never sees stale data.
A cold start is slower for a few minutes while the cache fills.

sections.title: A read checks the cache first and the database second
sections.text:
The API asks the cache for the order. On a hit it returns at once. On a miss it reads the row from the database, stores a copy in the cache and returns it.

A write updates the database and then removes the cached copy. The next read fills it again.

sections.title: Three parts make up the read path

items.title: API
items.text: Receives the read and decides where to look.

items.title: Cache
items.text: Holds recent orders in memory for quick reads.

items.title: Database
items.text: Stores every order and answers cache misses.
